one_month_reasoning: Window to 2026-11-19 holds: Q3 2026 results and the new 2027-2031 capital/financing plan on Oct 29 before the open (call notice [11]; management said on the Q2 call [6] the 5-year update comes with Q3); the Nov 3 US midterms (MN and CO statewide races matter for utility regulation); MN gas rate-case decision expected Nov 2026 and CO electric/gas and NM settlements expected Q3-Q4 2026 [2]; and the 10y UST, which rose from 4.67% (end-July) to 5.15-5.26% in October [16] and explains most of the ~8% slide since Q2. The plan roll-forward is usually a mild positive for rate-base growth (prior plan $60B base + $10B+ line of sight [3]), but new incremental capex comes with ~40% equity [3], which can offset; Q3 consensus $1.37 [15] is near guidance pace. With no clear directional edge I centre the month at ~$76.85 (+0.2%) with a 6% monthly sigma (19%/3.5 = 5.4% plus an earnings/plan-day bump). The WSJ report [18] on Anthropic's draft S-1 gives no pricing date; if the IPO lands in the window, any liquidity drain should hit AI-beta names more than a regulated utility, so I add no directional tilt for it.

fair_value.method: Rate-base EPS build (avg rate base x 53.5% equity x ~8.4% earned ROE, less HoldCo drag, over the forward-equity share path) gives NTM EPS $4.84 at the horizon; 17.5x (7% below the 18.85x peer median) = $84.58 weighted 0.8, blended with a driver DCF at 5.95% WACC / 3.5% g = $65.36 weighted 0.2 -> $80.74.

comps_summary.peer_range: NTM P/E 13.7x-21.5x (12 peers); NTM EV/EBITDA 9.6x-10.7x (4 peers with EBITDA consensus); EPS growth median +7.8% (5.7% to 18.3%)
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 17.5x NTM P/E at the horizon vs 18.85x median (-7%); XEL trades at 17.2x today (76.68 / NTM consensus $4.46). XEL TTM EV/EBITDA ~14.9x (EV $85.3B = 624.6M x $76.68 + $37.4B net debt, over F92 $5,720M) sits above the 4-peer NTM median 10.25x because XEL's EBITDA lags its 17% rate-base step-up in 2027; not used as a leg.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: Discount kept, not closed: (1) wildfire liability is un-legislated in Colorado (management calls it a 2027 priority [6]) and live in Texas (AG suit for damages and civil penalties [7]); (2) the plan needs $7B of equity (85% contracted [3]) plus ~40% equity on any incremental capex, so growth is partly diluted; (3) PSCo earns ~7.2% vs 9.3% allowed [3]. Against that, consensus EPS growth +10.2% (FY27/FY26 [15]) beats the 7.8% peer median, which is why I hold the discount at ~7% rather than ES-like levels. The discount narrows only on CO legislation (bull), not on growth alone.

thesis_break_reason: $61 is ~12.6x NTM EPS ($4.84), below the cheapest peer (ES 13.7x) and below the $65 zero-growth capitalised value: trading there would most likely mean a new at-fault wildfire with liability beyond insurance, a regulatory reset (ROE cuts / disallowed data-center capex) or an equity raise that breaks the 6-8%+ EPS guide, not ordinary rate-driven volatility (1-sigma 12-month move at 19% vol is ~$62-63 from today, so $61 sits just beyond it).

key_uncertainties: Rates: the group P/E moves with the 10y; a further +50bp is roughly -1.5 to -2 turns (the bear case).
Size of equity in the new 2027-2031 plan: incremental capex is funded ~40% with equity, so a bigger plan raises EPS growth less than rate base.
Earned ROE gap at PSCo (7.2% vs 9.3% allowed) and regulatory lag on a 17% rate-base step-up in 2027.
Conversion of the >20 GW data-center pipeline into signed ESAs (only ~2 GW contracted/under construction plus Google pending), and regulators' view of who bears stranded-cost risk.
Wildfire: Texas AG civil-penalty suit; a new at-fault fire in CO or the TX Panhandle before liability legislation passes.
Direct Anthropic exposure is unverified: the TeraWulf/Fluidstack Abernathy campus is in SPS territory (TeraWulf filing), but only a third-party tracker labels it an Anthropic site.

reverse_dcf_check: The 17.5x horizon P/E leg ($84.6) is reproduced by the engine DCF at a WACC of ~5.7% (vs 5.95% CAPM) with 3.5% terminal growth, i.e. it implies regulated returns capitalised at ~1.3x rate base EV and rate base growth of ~11-13% through 2030 then ~3.5%. That is plausible only if (a) the capex plan is executed with constructive orders (recent orders at 9.2-9.6% ROE support it), and (b) the 10y does not settle above ~5.5%; the post-horizon risks above (wildfire, backlash, data-center slowdown; net about -$1.2/sh probability-weighted) are what keep the multiple at a 7% discount rather than at the peer median.

reasoning: Primary-lane build. (1) Company documents give the spine: rate base $56B (2025) -> $66B/$77B/$86B/$90B/$94B on the $60B base plan, $10B+ line of sight lifting the CAGR to ~13% [3]; 2026 ongoing EPS guide $4.04-4.16 reaffirmed, 6-8%+ growth off $3.80 [2,4], with management now saying 9%+ through 2030 [6]; equity need $7B, 85% addressed [3]; the 10-Q shows 27.3M forward shares settling Dec-2026 to May-2027 and 42.5M Dec-2027 to Dec-2028 [1]. (2) Rate-base EPS: avg RB x 53.5% equity x earned ROE ~8.4% (TTM 8.43% [3]) less HoldCo drag gives $4.10/$4.50/$4.92 (FY26-28), within 1% of consensus $4.12/$4.54 [15]. (3) Valuation: 17.5x (7% under the 18.85x peer median [17]) on NTM EPS $4.84 = $84.6; driver DCF $65 at 5.95% WACC (10y 5.15% [16]); blended $80.7 per the 0.2 DCF weight. (4) Why the stock is $76.68: the 10y rose ~50-60bp since end-July [16] and utilities de-rated; XEL-specific overhangs are wildfire (TX AG suit [7]), equity funding, and data-center pushback (MN AG vs the Google ESA [13]). (5) WSJ/Anthropic [18]: the ~$450B of cloud commitments (up to $86B with Nscale/Lambda), >$600B total infrastructure and 'could spend $750B' raise the odds that XEL's >20 GW pipeline converts, and Anthropic's own S-1 says it is developing its own sites via third-party operators. A direct link in XEL territory exists only at one remove: TeraWulf's filing places its 168 MW (240 MW gross) Fluidstack campus at Abernathy, TX in SPS territory on SPP, with power passed through to the tenant [8]; Fluidstack is Anthropic's named builder for Texas [9]; only a tracker labels Abernathy an Anthropic site [14], so I do not treat it as verified. Counterparty risk: under XEL's large-load tariffs (CO: 15-yr, 80% minimum, six-month deposit, exit fee = remaining minimum bills [12]; TX filing: 15-yr+, security, exit charges) the customer carries stranded-cost risk during the contract, but six months of deposit is small against 15 years of generation capex, so a failed neocloud tenant would test the tariffs and push disputed costs into rate cases, i.e. a regulatory rather than a direct shareholder loss. Anthropic's risk factor on organised data-center opposition matches what is already visible in MN and CO, which can slow large-load approvals (Google decision early 2027). (6) On Kilian's IPO-liquidity question: XEL's holder base is yield/defensive, and the base plan carries little data-center load [6], so an IPO-driven drain from AI-beta names should touch XEL mainly through the 'AI power' basket; a flow-driven dip into the low $70s with rates stable and the plan intact would be a buying opportunity (fair value ~$81, 3.1% yield [10]); a drop driven by rates above ~5.5% or a new wildfire is not (thesis break $61). (7) Ladder: engine mixture (bear $63.8 p0.25 / base $80.7 p0.55 / bull $94.7 p0.20, 13% within-scenario vol) gives a median ~$79 and a 10-90 range of ~$60-$100, consistent with 19% realized vol; I add a little lower-tail weight for catastrophic wildfire. Price-only forecast: the ~$2.40 of dividends paid before the horizon is excluded.

model_inputs.structure_note: Regulated utility: value carried by a P/E leg (weight 0.8) on a rate-base EPS build (avg rate base x 53.5% equity ratio x earned ROE ~8.3-8.75% less HoldCo drag, divided by the forward-equity share path), plus a driver DCF (weight 0.2 per the forward-P/E band 15.0-19.6x; XEL at 17.2x NTM). Engine 'EBIT' = NOPAT incl. AFUDC (ongoing net income + after-tax interest) so the engine's NOPAT reproduces the EPS build; revenue is total operating revenue (fuel is pass-through, so margins are not economic margins). Capex is the $60B base plan by year plus $10B line-of-sight phased 2027-30; FY2030 capex is normalised to D&A + 3.5% x ~$103B rate base so the Gordon terminal starts from steady state (growth capex after 2029 assumed to earn about its cost of capital). Shares and net debt at the horizon are stated directly because the engine's bridge has no equity issuance. EV/EBITDA is not used as an engine leg because engine EBITDA is NOPAT-based; it is a narrative cross-check only. METHOD-FIT flag (no XBRL revenue/market cap) is a tagging artifact: revenue $14,669M comes from the Q4 2025 release and market cap from F89 x price, so it does not weaken the methods; the zero-growth capitalised-earnings leg is the added non-multiple check.
model_inputs.gap_note: fair_value.value equals the engine base horizon value.
model_inputs.dcf_check: DCF $65 is ~23% below the P/E leg ($85). The gap is the discount rate, not the cash flows: the peer P/E implies a WACC of ~5.7% (engine reverse DCF) vs 5.95% CAPM, and the DCF's terminal is 108% of EV because 2026-29 FCFF is deeply negative (capex 60-100% of revenue). Every 25bp of WACC moves the DCF ~$9/sh. Regulated utilities trade at ~1.3x rate base EV, i.e. the market capitalises regulated returns at a lower rate than CAPM with a 5.15% risk-free gives. I keep the playbook weight (0.2) rather than tuning the WACC to the multiples; it pulls the blend ~$4 below the P/E leg, a deliberate rates-risk haircut.

inputs_detail.derivation: Total operating revenues FY2025 (electric 12,160 + gas 2,452 + other 57) from the Q4 2025 release; not XBRL-tagged in the fact pack.
